title: Epochal session bundle format (draft)
content:
Purpose
---
Short notes on an "epochal" approach to session checkpointing and restore. Goal: make client-visible session checkpoints that are small, streamable, appendable, and partial-restorable so interactive clients (web/mobile/edge) can resume with minimal token re-synthesis and bounded latency. This is a personal draft; thinking is intentionally informal and includes experiments, tradeoffs, and open questions.

High-level idea
---
- Each session has a base snapshot (optional) plus an ordered sequence of epochs.
- An epoch contains a compact delta: new user/assistant turns, KV-cache deltas (chunked), and pointer metadata.
- Clients can request: latest manifest, specific epoch ranges, or a streaming resume that applies epochs in order and then requests live traffic.
- Bundles are self-describing, signed, and support partial repair/retry of missing chunks.

Why epochal vs monolithic snapshot
---
- Monolithic checkpoints grow quickly and are expensive to upload/download.
- Epochal bundles allow incremental upload during a session and small-range restore for reconnect.
- Enables deduping common initial context across sessions by sharing base snapshots.

Bundle layout (on-disk / object store)
---
Top-level path: sessions/{session_id}/bundles/{bundle_id}/
- manifest.json               # short descriptor (required)
- base.bin                   # optional base full state (when present)
- epochs/                    # directory of epoch files
  - 00000001.meta            # human/codec metadata for epoch
  - 00000001.data            # compressed payload (chunked)
  - 00000002.meta
  - 00000002.data
- blobs/                     # optional large blobs (embedding caches, media)
  - blob-<sha256>.zst
- signatures/                # manifest + bundle-level signatures
  - manifest.sig
  - epochs.sig
- index.json                 # optional precomputed index for quick range reads

Manifest fields (example)
---
{"version":"0.2","bundle_id":"bndl-20251104-ashap","session_id":"s-8a9f","created_at":"2025-11-04T15:32:21Z","base_present":false,"epoch_count":37,"epochs":["00000001","00000002"],"compression":"zstd","chunk_size":65536,"signer":"kms:projects/redwood/keys/ephemeral-restore","hash_algo":"blake3"}

Note: manifest itself should be small (<4KB) and should include signed manifest.sig for quick trust checks.

Epoch file semantics
---
- .meta (text) contains: epoch_id, prev_epoch (or base), sequence_number, client_event_bounds (start_idx,end_idx), approximate_token_count, pointers to blobs, corruption_map (optional).
- .data is a stream of framed records. Each frame: [frame-header][payload]. Frame-header = 16 bytes: {frame_type:u8, flags:u8, chunk_index:u32, payload_len:u32, reserved:u16}.
- Frame types: 0x01=turn-delta (json), 0x02=kv-delta (binary), 0x03=embedding-blob-ref, 0x04=padding/placeholder.
- Each payload chunk is compressed (zstd) and has per-chunk blake3 digest appended in a trailer so we can repair single chunks via range requests.

Minimal epoch payload example (pseudoblob):
---
[frame 0] turn-delta -> {"turn_id":"t-203","speaker":"user","text":"Where did I leave my keys?","timestamp":"2025-11-04T15:31:05Z"}
[frame 1] turn-delta -> {"turn_id":"t-204","speaker":"assistant","text":"You mentioned earlier: keys are probably on the kitchen counter.","refers_to_turn":"t-97"}
[frame 2] kv-delta -> binary blob encoding small KV edits to attention/KV cache (chunked)

API shapes (draft)
---
Note: these are sketch endpoints for session resume and snapshot management. Auth/Authorization omitted for brevity.

1) Publish epoch (append)
POST /v1/sessions/{session_id}/bundles/{bundle_id}/epochs
Headers: Content-Type: application/octet-stream; X-Epoch-Id: 00000037; X-Chunk-Index: 0/1/..; X-Frame-Seq: 12
Body: raw framed binary chunk (possibly with multiple frames)
Response: 202 Accepted + {"received":"ok","epoch_id":"00000037","chunk_index":0}

Behavior: server assembles chunks into epoch.data and publishes epoch.meta when all chunks received. If chunk missing for >30s, epoch is marked partial and manifest updated with corruption_map.

2) Fetch manifest
GET /v1/sessions/{session_id}/bundles/{bundle_id}/manifest
Response: manifest.json (signed) 200

3) Streamed restore (client side)
POST /v1/sessions/{session_id}/resume?from_epoch=00000020&to=latest
Request: client indicates its last-seen epoch/turn and wants to replay deltas
Response: 200 Stream (Transfer-Encoding: chunked) -> sequence of framed records (same internal frame format). Server ensures epochs delivered in-order. At stream end, server sends a 'handoff' frame indicating live routing start and an idempotency token.

4) Partial range fetch
GET /v1/sessions/{session_id}/bundles/{bundle_id}/epochs/00000022.data?chunk=3
Response: bytes with Content-Range and chunk digest header; status 206

Restore semantics
---
- Client applies frames in-order. For kv-delta frames, client merges deterministic patch; patches must be commutative within an epoch to support reordering of chunk reception (but epoch-level ordering remains strict).
- If any chunk is missing/corrupt the server may: return an explicit 'gap' frame pointing to a repair URL; client can request the missing chunk(s) over a separate endpoint.
- For streaming resume, the server provides a 'fast-forward' abbreviated state for large KV (e.g., key bloom filter + missing-keys list) so client can continue with degraded but correct behavior until full repair completes.

Versioning and compatibility
---
- manifest.version is the compatibility marker. We support convertors on the server to expose new fields to older clients where possible.
- epoch file format is versioned in .meta (format_version). Readers must be tolerant: unknown frame_types should be ignored with a log-level and optional metric.

Integrity and security
---
- Chunk-level blake3 digests + manifest-level KMS signature. KMS key rotation supported via manifests pointing to signer version.
- All blobs encrypted at rest using envelope encryption; per-bundle DEK wrapped by KMS. For private deployments, signer can be HSM-backed.

Compression & chunking heuristics
---
- Default chunk_size: 64KiB for general payloads. For KV blobs we may choose 256KiB chunks to reduce header overhead.
- If a frame is > chunk_size, we split into contiguous chunk frames with sub-frame sequence numbers. This allows streaming and backpressure across poor mobile net.

Retention, pruning, and GC
---
- Server-side: keep last N bundles per session (configurable) + TTL. Older bundles eligible for cold storage or deletion.
- Client-side: clients should store a small cache of last applied epoch_id (idempotency token) so reconnects can resume from server delta without reuploading local drafts.

Migration from existing snapshot formats
---
- Map existing monolithic snapshot -> base.bin + synthetic epochs (replay the entire monolith as a single epoch with chunking).
- A server-side migration job can ingest old snapshots and emit new bundles with signatures.

Operational signals & metrics
---
- metrics to emit: epoch_publish_latency, epoch_repair_rate, avg_chunks_per_epoch, percent_partial_epochs, resume_success_rate, average_resume_time(ms), failed-signature-count.

Open questions (needs team input)
---
- Should we allow client-side direct upload to cloud storage for large blobs (multipart upload) or always funnel through route service? Tradeoffs: client security vs offload traffic.
- How to handle multi-device concurrent session edits (merge model)? For now: optimistic last-writer-on-server with per-turn causal ids; future: CRDT-like merge for agent state.
- Which fields are allowed in .meta to be mutable after publish? (corruption_map vs token_count)
- Performance: empirical numbers for chunk size tradeoffs on 3G mobile vs datacenter. We need a bench matrix.

Edge cases & notes
---
- If client reconnects and uploads epoch n that already exists, server should return 409 and an idempotency token; allow client to re-attach chunks to existing epoch to finish partial ones.
- For privacy, avoid storing raw PII in manifest indexes; manifests should keep pointers but not plaintext text snippets unless explicitly opted-in.

Next steps / action items
---
- [Asha] implement prototype encoder that can emit framed epoch files from an existing in-memory session (local dev tool). (due: 2026-01-15)
- [Daniel] spike network cost: measure upload bandwidth for chunk_size {32k,64k,256k} on iOS/Android emulators. (due: 2026-01-22)
- [Lina] draft server-side repairs API and auth model for direct S3/multipart. (due: 2026-01-29)
- Convene 30m sync with SRE + security to validate KMS/signature approach (provisional invite: slack thread show above).

Rough sketch (ASCII)
---
client                               server/storage
  |-- POST chunk -> /epochs/00000037.data (chunk 0) --> assemble --> store --> manifest update
  |-- POST chunk -> /epochs/00000037.data (chunk 1) --> assemble --> store
  |-- POST commit -> /epochs/00000037.meta (complete)
  |  
  |-- GET /resume?from=00000020 -> stream frames ---> apply in-order -> live traffic

Appendix: example .meta (text)
---
version: 0.2
epoch_id: 00000037
format_version: 1
prev_epoch: 00000036
sequence_number: 37
start_turn_idx: 203
end_turn_idx: 207
approx_tokens: 482
frames: 18
chunk_count: 3
compression: zstd
blobs: ["blob-4f2b.."]
corruption_map: []

Open todo: make canonical proto for meta and frame header. Keep this doc as working notes until we agree on a first cut that SRE can run for 2-week dogfood.

End of draft.
